- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. Trail: feat(strategy): link commits to sessions by process identity
  Number:  1061
  ID:      01M08AZPPMGCYSCYDEA1D8K06Q
  Branch:  feat/session-identity-linking
  Base:    main
  Status:  open
  Author:  peyton-alt
  Phase:   building
  URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1061
  Assignees: peyton-alt
  Type:      task
  Created: 2026-08-17T17:05:55Z
  Updated: 2026-08-20T22:31:03Z

Description:
Problem:
Agent-made commits in worktree configurations weren't correctly attributed to their originating sessions. When an agent made a commit from a sibling worktree (a different git worktree in the same repository), the system relied solely on worktree path matching to link commits to sessions. This caused commits to either lose session linkage or, in cases of leaked test fixture sessions, to incorrectly link to the wrong session—producing dangling or malformed checkpoint trailers. The root issue: process identity wasn't being tracked, so there was no way to attribute a commit to the specific agent that made it across worktree boundaries.
Solution:
The branch introduces process-identity-based commit attribution that records the agent process's identity (PID + start time) at session start, then matches it at commit time to link commits to their originating sessions regardless of worktree. Key changes:
Process ancestry tracking (proctree package, new): Captures the agent process identity—the first non-shell ancestor—to guard against PID reuse and filter out shared user-side infrastructure (shells, tmux, terminal emulator, IDE).
Identity-first linking (session_identity.go, new): Commit hooks walk their ancestry and match against recorded agent processes. Nearest ancestor wins; ties go to the most recently interacting session. This makes agent commits link to their own session in any worktree without relying on path bookkeeping.
Guest-linked commits: When a commit identity-matches outside the session's home worktree, it condenses and links but preserves worktree-coupled state (BaseCommit, shadow-branch realignment) on the session's home worktree only.
Fallback worktree matching: Commits with no recorded agent in their ancestry (human commits) continue to use worktree-path matching, now with liveness filtering to resolve ambiguity across multiple worktrees.
Test isolation safeguards: Session state store now refuses to open outside the temp root under go test, failing loudly when tests lack proper repo isolation to prevent fixture leaks.
Human commits remain unaffected; agent commits now link correctly across worktrees.

Trail: fix(doctor): hint --force instead of crashing on stuck sessions with no TTY
  Number:  1064
  ID:      01M08G7R841C34XB31EP5M6W75
  Branch:  fix/doctor-stuck-session-no-tty
  Base:    main
  Status:  open
  Author:  peyton-alt
  Phase:   building
  URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1064
  Assignees: peyton-alt
  Type:      task
  Created: 2026-08-17T18:37:42Z
  Updated: 2026-08-20T22:57:10Z

Description:
Problem:
The entire doctor command would crash with "could not open TTY" errors when run in non-interactive environments (agents, CI) because it tried to open TTY prompts without checking if an interactive terminal was available. Stuck sessions and disconnected metadata checks would fail instead of providing useful diagnostics.
Solution:
Added guards to check interactive.CanPromptInteractively() before opening any TTY prompts in the doctor command. When running non-interactively, the command now:
Displays each stuck session's diagnosis (no early exit after the first one)
Shows what action --force would take on each session (condense or discard)
Hints users to run entire doctor --force to apply fixes
Leaves sessions untouched for later interactive processing
Degrades gracefully for disconnected metadata checks with the same hint
Updated help text to document the non-interactive behavior and added tests to verify sessions are diagnosed without crashes and remain intact for manual action.

Trail: feat: self-heal zombie sessions via detached sweep from session-start
  Number:  1073
  ID:      01M08RYSC441VSR8KHGPTXE5BH
  Branch:  feat/zombie-session-sweep
  Base:    main
  Status:  open
  Author:  peyton-alt
  Phase:   building
  URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1073
  Assignees: peyton-alt
  Type:      task
  Created: 2026-08-17T21:10:05Z
  Updated: 2026-08-20T22:02:52Z

Description:
Problem: Abandoned sessions (zombies) accumulate when an agent process dies without properly stopping the session, or when an ended session sits uncondensed for over 24 hours. These sessions remain as stale state and shadow branches on disk, cluttering the repository and consuming resources.
Solution: Add a background zombie-session sweep that runs detached from the session-start hook to automatically repair abandoned sessions. The sweep identifies two types of zombies: (1) active sessions whose owning agent process has exited, which are finalized immediately, and (2) ended uncondensed sessions older than 24 hours, which are condensed using the existing engine. The sweep is throttled to run at most once per 15-minute window per repository to avoid spawning duplicate processes during rapid session activity. Imported sessions are excluded since they are permanent historical records with no condensation data. The sweep is best-effort—failed sessions are logged and retried on the next spawn window. A new hidden __sweep_sessions command executes the sweep detached with file-based logging for diagnosability. The session-start hook conditionally spawns this command when zombie sessions are detected, keeping the hook latency unaffected since the sweep runs in the background.

commit 8581735744a91586c16517a499ead6e1b3951814
Author: Peyton Montei <peyton@entire.io>
Date:   Mon Aug 17 17:09:51 2026 -0700

    refactor(strategy): converge identity linking on proclive, delete proctree
    
    Trail review (1061) found internal/proctree duplicating the existing
    proclive package: same ancestry walk, same per-platform introspection
    (one sysctl/stat parse apart), and — decisively — proclive's Identity is
    already persisted on EVERY turn start as SessionState.Owner by
    captureSessionOwner, seven lines from where this branch re-walked the
    same process tree into a second field. The review also showed the
    duplicate's Windows walker ran in no CI job (the Windows job filters on
    test names carrying Windows/MSYS; none did), had an orphan-reparenting
    hazard PID recycling makes real, cost one process-table snapshot per
    ancestry level, and that the shell filter was missing "entire" and "go"
    — both already on proclive's transient list.
    
    Converge instead of duplicating:
    
    - proclive gains HasAncestor(Identity) — the commit-attribution
      question ("was this process spawned, however indirectly, by the
      recorded owner?") with proclive's host, boot, and start-fingerprint
      guards, so a recycled PID or an identity recorded on another machine
      can never match — two guards the deleted package lacked (its own doc
      conceded the Linux cross-reboot collision that proclive's bootID
      closes). Plus IdentityOf(pid) for callers and tests.
    - findSessionByCommitAncestry matches SessionState.Owner via
      HasAncestor. No new recording, no AgentAncestry field, no
      refreshAgentAncestry (Owner is re-captured every turn start, which
      already covers resume under a new agent process). Ties — one agent
      process hosting several sessions, or a nested agent whose outer agent
      is also an ancestor — go to the most recently interacting session.
    - internal/proctree is deleted. On platforms proclive cannot introspect
      (Windows), identity matching reports nothing and linking falls back
      to worktree matching — honestly, rather than via platform code no CI
      job executed.
    
    This also positions PR #1777 (cross-common-dir auto-adopt): its
    owner-matching compares first-non-transient identities and breaks when
    a non-transient wrapper interposes at commit time; HasAncestor's
    any-ancestor semantics are immune and reusable there.

735	
736	The manual-commit strategy (`manual_commit*.go`) does not modify the active branch - no commits are created on the working branch. Instead it:
737	
738	- Creates shadow branch `entire/<HEAD-commit-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>` per base commit + worktree
739	- **Worktree-specific branches** - each git worktree gets its own shadow branch namespace, preventing conflicts
740	- **Supports multiple concurrent sessions** - checkpoints from different sessions in the same directory interleave on the same shadow branch
741	- Condenses session logs to permanent `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on user commits
742	- Every path that builds a stored transcript sanitizes before redacting; the committed paths also externalize images in between, giving **sanitize → externalize images → redact**. Sanitization is the agent's optional `agent.TranscriptSanitizer` capability, applied via `agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage`; it strips non-portable agent state (Codex's encrypted reasoning payloads and compaction blobs, which are bound to the originating session and cannot be replayed out of a checkpoint). The three paths are the Stop/shadow write (`lifecycle.go` sanitizes before `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` is written, then the metadata-dir walker redacts it into the shadow tree — **no externalization**, so inline images in a shadow transcript are subject to redaction and assets exist only under committed checkpoints), post-commit condensation (`prepareTranscriptForStorage` in `manual_commit_condensation.go`), and the Stop finalize full-session rewrite (`manual_commit_hooks.go`). Where all three steps run, order is load-bearing at each step: sanitizing first avoids externalizing images out of items about to be discarded (storing an asset whose referencing line disappears) and avoids redacting megabytes of ciphertext only to discard it — base64 is the pathological input for the entropy layer, so a large Codex rollout otherwise costs tens of seconds per Stop *and* per commit; externalizing before redaction is required because redaction would otherwise flag and destroy the high-entropy base64. Sanitization is idempotent, so downstream paths call it without knowing whether an upstream path already did (`checkpoint.sanitizeForAgentType` is the store's belt-and-braces call). The agent's own transcript is never modified. Coupling to respect: `SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize` is a growth baseline compared against the shadow transcript blob size in `sessionHasNewContent`, so it must be measured in the same sanitized (pre-externalization) coordinate — that is `CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline`; using the raw size makes the comparison false forever and the session silently stops condensing.
743	- Each committed session stores the (sanitized, redacted) transcript (`full.jsonl`, read by CLI resume/explain) plus a best-effort compact transcript (`transcript.jsonl`, generated via `transcript/compact`). Like `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl` stores the **full compacted session** on every checkpoint (via `compact.FullWithBoundary`), so each checkpoint is self-contained and the session survives a mid-history checkpoint being lost/reverted/rebased. This checkpoint's slice begins at the session metadata's `compact_transcript_start` (a line offset in compact-output coordinates, distinct from `checkpoint_transcript_start` which indexes raw `full.jsonl` lines); a nil/absent marker means a legacy delta-only `transcript.jsonl` (read from line 0). The marker rounds toward inclusion when a streaming message straddles the boundary, so the slice never drops this checkpoint's content but may repeat ≤1 merged line at its head. Compact generation is best-effort and is skipped when the compacted output exceeds the 50MB blob cap (unlike `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl` is not chunked — `full.jsonl` stays authoritative and the compact is regenerable); in the OPF finalize rewrite a failed/skipped regeneration drops the prior `transcript.jsonl` and clears the marker rather than shipping a stale, less-redacted compact. Both files are pushed with the v1 branch. The root `metadata.json` `sessions[].transcript` pointer keeps targeting `full.jsonl`; when the compact transcript was generated the session entry also carries a `compact_transcript` path pointing at `transcript.jsonl` (omitted otherwise) so external readers can locate it next to `full.jsonl`.

747	- **Location-independent transcript resolution** - transcript paths are always computed dynamically from the current repo location (via `agent.GetSessionDir` + `agent.ResolveSessionFile`), never stored in checkpoint metadata. This ensures restore/rewind works after repo relocation or across machines.
748	- **Token usage scoping** - `SessionState.TokenUsage` is the session-wide total used by `entire status`; `SessionState.CheckpointTokenUsage` is the pending checkpoint delta since the last condensation. Checkpoint metadata must stay scoped to `CheckpointTranscriptStart` or the pending checkpoint delta. Cursor tokens come only from stop-hook payloads, while Copilot CLI can also backfill full-session totals from `session.shutdown`. Condensation's transcript recompute runs with `subagentsDir=""` and so drops `SubagentTokens`; `withSubagentTokensFrom` refills it from the already-rescoped `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`, and the store sums it across a checkpoint's sessions via `types.AddTokenUsage` (the single token-summing primitive — do not hand-roll another; a field-by-field copy is how the nested total came to be dropped in the first place).

+owner are out of scope, matching doctor's boundary. The 7-day stale-session
+purge bounds the sweep's window: a zombie that stays unfixed past 7 days is
+removed by the purge, not the sweep. See `cmd/entire/cli/session_sweep.go`.

+

+(`strategy/session_identity.go`): the **worktree-matched set** (every session

+by design) **plus the identity-matched session** when the committing process's
+ancestry names one that path matching missed.

+records — `SessionState.Owner`, a `proclive.Identity` captured on every turn
+start by `captureSessionOwner` (the first non-transient ancestor of the hook:
+agents run hooks as children, possibly via `sh -c`, and proclive skips
+shells, the `entire` binary itself, and the Go toolchain). At commit time the
+hook snapshots its ancestry once (`proclive.CurrentAncestry`) and asks
+`Ancestry.Depth(owner)` per candidate: was this commit's process spawned,
+however indirectly, by that session's agent? Snapshotting once matters — the
+shared store holds one state file per session, so a per-candidate walk would
+repeat the hostname, boot-id, and proc reads dozens of times per commit.
+Host, boot, and start-time guards mean a recycled PID or an identity recorded
+on another machine can never match. The nearest ancestor wins, so a nested
+agent is attributed over the outer agent that spawned it; only sessions
+matching at the same depth (one agent process hosting several sessions) fall
+back to the most recently interacting one. On platforms proclive cannot introspect (Windows),
+identity matching reports nothing and linking falls back to worktree
+matching. This makes an agent-made commit link to
+its own session **in any worktree**, with no bookkeeping to drift. A commit
+identity-matched outside the session's home worktree is **guest-linked**: it
+condenses and links, but never mutates worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`,
+shadow-branch realignment) — those follow only the session's own worktree HEAD.
+

+no recorded agent in their ancestry — human commits, detached runners): exact
+`WorktreePath` match first, then sessions from a sibling worktree of the same
+repo, provided they resolve to a single worktree. Imported sessions (`Kind=imported`) never link —
+they are historical records. When candidates span several worktrees, sessions
+that interacted within the last 15 minutes are preferred; if a single live
+worktree remains it links, otherwise the hook declines with a stderr hint

+worktrees are never guessed between).

+linking and produced a dangling `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.

content.text:
I read all three branches, built and ran the affected package tests locally on each, and confirmed all three PRs are green on CI (#2013, #2015, #2029).

---

## 1061 — `feat(strategy): link commits to sessions by process identity` (#2013)

The core design is right: union-not-precedence between worktree and identity matching, nearest-ancestor-wins, host/boot/start-time guards, one ancestry snapshot per commit instead of per candidate. Deleting `internal/proctree` in favour of `proclive` was the correct call — `SessionState.Owner` was already being captured on every turn start seven lines away. Docs are unusually good.

**1. The guest path retains the shadow branch but still resets the checkpoint window** — `manual_commit_hooks.go:1416-1444`

The guest branch calls `resetCheckpointWindow(state)` (which sets `StepCount = 0`) and then returns *before* `shadowBranchesToDelete[shadowBranchName]` and before advancing `BaseCommit`. Two consequences:

- `CondenseSession` recomputes the shadow branch from `state.BaseCommit` + `state.WorktreeID` and reads the branch **tip tree**. Since the guest condense neither deletes the branch nor moves `BaseCommit`, the same shadow content stays eligible to be condensed again into the next checkpoint this session links to. The home path avoids this precisely by deleting the branch and advancing `BaseCommit` to a new branch name.
- `StepCount == 0` un-pins the branch. `cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused` (`manual_commit_condensation.go:1471`) and `doctor.go:690` both gate on `state.StepCount > 0` to decide "another session still needs this branch", and `isWarnableStaleEndedSession` / `classifySession` (`doctor.go:289`) both bail on `StepCount <= 0`. So between a guest condense and the session's next `SaveStep`, a concurrent session sharing the branch can delete it, and if the session ends in that window its shadow branch is orphaned without doctor flagging it.

The comment justifies retaining the branch by the carry-forward hazard — but carry-forward is already gated separately by `isSessionHomeWorktree(repoDir, state)` at line 1327. So the retention looks like belt-and-braces that now contradicts the `StepCount` reset. Either skip `resetCheckpointWindow` for guests, or schedule the branch for deletion (its content just landed in the guest checkpoint).

**2. `condenseAndUpdateState`'s variadic makes "guest" the default** — line 1428

```go
var isHome bool
if len(opts) > 0 { isHome = isSessionHomeWorktree(opts[0].repoDir, state) }
```

Both current callers pass `condenseOpts`, so this is latent — but a caller that omits it silently gets guest treatment (no branch cleanup, no `BaseCommit` advance, `FilesTouched` never cleared). For a variadic that's the wrong fail-safe direction. Make `repoDir` a positional parameter, or default `isHome = true`.

**3. `isSessionHomeWorktree` uses raw `==` on paths** — `session_identity.go:121`

`reconcileWorktreePathForResumedTurn` in the same package compares worktree paths with `filepath.Clean`. In practice both sides come from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` so they agree today, but path equality now gates *state mutation* rather than just matching, so the failure mode of a mismatch is worse than it was. Cheap to harden.

**4. The ambiguity hint can fire once per replayed commit during a rebase** — `session_identity.go:44`

The stderr hint lives inside `findSessionsForCommitLinking`, which `PostCommit` also calls. `PostCommit` resolves the trailer first and only computes `isRebase := isGitSequenceOperation(ctx)` *after* the find, so a `git rebase` replaying N trailer-bearing commits in a worktree with ambiguous sessions prints the hint N times. Suppressing it when `isGitSequenceOperation` is true, or only emitting from `PrepareCommitMsg`, would fix it.

**5. Test coverage stops short of the riskiest code.** `session_identity_test.go` covers the matcher, the union, imported exclusion, ambiguity/liveness and `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` gating — but nothing exercises the guest branch of `condenseAndUpdateState` or the carry-forward gate, which is where the "would replace the home worktree's in-flight state with foreign files" hazard the comments describe actually lives.

Two things worth stating in the PR description rather than fixing:

- The guest gate is **path-based, not identity-based**, so it also changes the pre-existing cross-worktree *fallback* path. That's an improvement (the fallback used to rewrite `BaseCommit` from a foreign worktree and orphan the home shadow branch), but the docs frame guest-linking as identity-only, and this is the behaviour change most likely to surface in existing repos.
- `resolveWorktreeCandidates` now links where the old code declined: one live worktree within 15 minutes wins. Two live worktrees where one is mid-long-build (>15 min idle) now silently links to the other. Reasonable trade for #1852, but it's a guess the previous code refused to make, and `recentSessionWindow` should be called out as the knob it is.

---

## 1064 — `fix(doctor): hint --force instead of crashing` (#2015)

Clean, and correctly modelled on the existing `checkGitHooks` degrade — same guard, same wording, same "return nil" semantics. It reuses `canCondenseStuckSession` for the hint rather than re-deriving it, so the disclosed fix can't drift from what `--force` actually does. Nothing blocking. Three small things:

- `confirmDoctorFix` got an internal safety net; `promptSessionAction` didn't. That asymmetry is the one thing a future call site could trip over — worth either adding the same guard or a comment saying why it isn't needed.
- Non-interactive runs still exit 0 with stuck sessions reported. Consistent with `checkGitHooks`, so presumably deliberate — but if anyone wants `entire doctor` usable as a CI gate, now is when to say so.
- Tests only cover the non-interactive path (the `go test` default). That matches repo norms; just noting the interactive branch has no pin.

---

## 1073 — `feat: self-heal zombie sessions via detached sweep` (#2029)

**1. The predicate never nominates IDLE dead-owner sessions — the case the design calls the common one** — `session_sweep.go:36`

```go
if st.Phase.IsActive() { return st.OwnerExited() }
```

`Phase.IsActive()` is `p == PhaseActive` only (`session/phase.go:47`). An IDLE state falls through the imported check to `st.Phase != session.PhaseEnded → return false`. But `runSessionSweep`'s first action is `finalizeExitedSessions(ctx, states)`, which keys on `OwnerExited()` and *does* cover IDLE. So the sweep can fix IDLE zombies but will never be spawned for a repo whose only zombies are IDLE.

CLAUDE.md is explicit about this being the case that matters: "**`OwnerExited` deliberately covers IDLE as well as ACTIVE** — an agent that finishes its last turn and then quits leaves IDLE, so gating on ACTIVE alone missed the common case." The new doc paragraph asserts the opposite — "IDLE sessions with a dead owner are out of scope, matching doctor's boundary" — and that justification doesn't hold: `entire doctor` calls the same `finalizeExitedSessions`, so doctor's boundary *includes* IDLE. Fix is one line: `if !st.IsEnded() { return st.OwnerExited() }`.

Relatedly, the `"idle session is never a zombie"` test case has no `Owner` at all, so `OwnerExited()` is false regardless of phase — it doesn't exercise the case its name claims.

**2. The detached sweep inherits a budget whose whole rationale is an interactive caller** — `session_finalize.go:15-31`

`sweepCondenseBudget = 1 * time.Second`, justified in its own doc comment by "the callers here are interactive commands — including `entire status --json` ... where nothing prints until the sweep returns." `__sweep_sessions` exists precisely so nobody is waiting, yet it gets the same 1s cap, and the 15-minute spawn throttle sits on top. A post-upgrade backlog therefore drains at roughly 1s of condensing per 15 minutes — which undercuts the feature's headline claim. Parameterize the budget for the detached path, or say in the PR why 1s is still right there.

**3. Throttle failure mode is "spawn every time"** — `session_sweep.go:236`

```go
if commonDir, cerr := session.GetGitCommonDir(ctx); cerr == nil && sweepRecentlySpawned(commonDir, time.Now()) { return }
```

A `GetGitCommonDir` error skips the throttle entirely — one detached child per session start, which is exactly what the throttle exists to prevent. `recentlySpawnedMarker`'s "never worse than before this guard existed" is true for the trail refresh but understates it here, where the guard is the only thing bounding fork count.

**4. The O(N) work happens before the throttle check.** Every session start reads every state file in the shared dir and runs a `proclive` probe per ACTIVE session, then checks the throttle. Reordering isn't free — `recentlySpawnedMarker` *records* on a miss, so a read-only variant would be needed first — but the current ordering deserves a comment saying it's deliberate, given this repo's open hook-latency floor.

Things done well and worth keeping: the condense-only contract with the explicit "discards are doctor's" boundary, the imported-session guard (with the reason spelled out), the re-load-and-re-check under the lock before acting, `IsCondensableEndedSession`'s note that it's a re-check for PostCommit but the *primary* check for the sweep, and `ensureLogger` + logging the top-level error in the detached child.

---

## Cross-cutting

- **1061 and 1073 merge cleanly except for one docs conflict**: both insert a paragraph at the same anchor in `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md`. All Go files auto-merge. Whichever lands second just needs the doc rebase.
- **`SessionState.Owner` is becoming a single point of failure for three behaviours**: liveness (already shipped), commit attribution (1061), and background sweeping (1073). It's nil on Windows and whenever hook ancestry resolves to only transient processes. Do we have any signal on how often `ResolveOwner` actually succeeds across the supported agents? Both PRs degrade correctly when it's nil, but the value of both features is proportional to a resolve rate nobody has measured.
- 1061's `ensureTestIsolatedStateDir` hard-fails `session.NewStateStore` under `go test` outside the temp root. That's the right call and CI is green, but it raises the bar for every future test touching session state — worth a line in the PR so it isn't discovered as a mystery failure.

Status:    resolved

Boot ID asymmetry causes false negatives when `bootID()` fails. If `CurrentAncestry` cannot read the boot ID (line 242 sets `boot = ""`), but a recorded session owner has a boot ID (captured on a previous successful read), `Ancestry.Depth` rejects the match at line 273 (`a.boot == "" || a.boot != id.Boot`). This means a session owner that was correctly fingerprinted with a boot ID will never match on the same machine after a transient boot-ID read failure, causing identity linking to silently fall back to worktree matching and potentially losing linkage. The guard should allow a match when the snapshot has no boot (`a.boot == ""`) and only reject when both are present but differ.

entire trail finding add --trail 1061 --severity medium --confidence 0.8 \
  --file cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go --line 1435 \
  -m 'The guest path resets the checkpoint window but keeps the shadow branch, so the same shadow content stays condensable and the branch loses its pin. `condenseAndUpdateState` line 1435 calls `resetCheckpointWindow(state)` (which sets `StepCount = 0`, manual_commit_git.go:396) and returns at 1444, before line 1448 marks the branch for deletion and before `BaseCommit` advances at 1450.

Two consequences:

1. Re-condensation. `CondenseSession` recomputes the branch from `state.BaseCommit` + `state.WorktreeID` (manual_commit_condensation.go:273) and reads the branch tip tree via `extractOrCreateSessionData` (:592). Because the guest path neither deletes the branch nor moves `BaseCommit`, the identical tip stays eligible to be condensed again into the next checkpoint this session links to. The home path avoids exactly this by pairing `StepCount = 0` with branch deletion plus a new branch name.

2. Lost pin. `StepCount > 0` is what makes a session claim its shadow branch: `cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused` (manual_commit_condensation.go:1471) and doctor.go:690 both use it to decide "another session still needs this branch", and `isWarnableStaleEndedSession` (manual_commit_session.go:131) plus `classifySession` (doctor.go:289) both bail on `StepCount <= 0`. Between a guest condense and the session next `SaveStep`, a concurrent session sharing the branch can delete it, and a session that ends in that window leaves an orphaned shadow branch that doctor will not flag.

The comment at 1417-1425 justifies retaining the branch by the carry-forward hazard, but carry-forward is already gated separately by `isSessionHomeWorktree(repoDir, state)` at line 1327 — so the retention is belt-and-braces that now contradicts the `StepCount` reset.

Fix: either skip `resetCheckpointWindow` on the guest path, or add `shadowBranchesToDelete[shadowBranchName] = struct{}{}` before returning (its content just landed in the guest checkpoint).

Verify: guest-condense a session, then assert the shadow ref still exists with `StepCount == 0`, and that a second commit produces a checkpoint containing the same files.' 2>&1 | tail -8

var isHome bool
if len(opts) > 0 {

`isSessionHomeWorktree` (session_identity.go:121) tests only whether the commit worktree equals the session worktree. Nothing in it is identity-specific. So a session matched by the *old* fallback — `findSessionsForWorktreeFromStates` returning a single-worktree sibling match, which has existed since before this branch — now also gets guest treatment: `BaseCommit` no longer advances (manual_commit_hooks.go:1499), the shadow branch is no longer deleted, carry-forward is skipped (:1327).

This is the behaviour change most likely to show up in an existing user repo (any multi-worktree setup, no agent ancestry required), so it belongs in the description explicitly.

**2. The liveness filter links where the old code deliberately declined.**

`resolveWorktreeCandidates` (manual_commit_session.go:264) now filters multi-worktree candidates to those that interacted within `recentSessionWindow` (15 min) and links if a single worktree survives. Previously any multi-worktree ambiguity declined outright.

entire trail finding add --trail 1073 --severity high --confidence 0.9 \
  --file cmd/entire/cli/session_sweep.go --line 36 \
  -m 'The predicate never nominates IDLE dead-owner sessions — the case the design calls the common one — while the sweep it gates does fix them.

```go
if st.Phase.IsActive() {
    return st.OwnerExited()
}
```

`Phase.IsActive()` is `p == PhaseActive` only (session/phase.go:47-49). An IDLE state therefore falls past line 37, past the imported guard at :43, and hits `st.Phase != session.PhaseEnded` at :46 → returns false. So `countSweepableZombies` (:172) counts it as zero and `maybeSpawnSessionSweep` (:228) never spawns.

But `runSessionSweep` first action is `finalizeExitedSessions(ctx, states)` (:97), which keys on `OwnerExited()` — and that covers IDLE. Net effect: the sweep is *capable* of fixing IDLE zombies but will never be spawned for a repo whose only zombies are IDLE.

CLAUDE.md is explicit that this is the case that matters: "**`OwnerExited` deliberately covers IDLE as well as ACTIVE** — an agent that finishes its last turn and then quits leaves IDLE, so gating on ACTIVE alone missed the common case; only already-finalized sessions are excluded, per the shared `State.IsEnded()` predicate."

The new doc paragraph (docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md) asserts the opposite — "IDLE sessions with a dead owner are out of scope, matching doctor boundary" — and that justification does not hold: `entire doctor` reaches the same zombies through the same `finalizeExitedSessions` (doctor.go:162), so doctor boundary *includes* IDLE.

Fix: `if !st.IsEnded() { return st.OwnerExited() }`, i.e. the same predicate `finalizeExitedSessions` uses, so nomination and action agree.

Verify: state with `Phase: PhaseIdle` and a dead-owner fixture → `isSweepableZombie` should be true; today it is false.' 2>&1 | tail -5

`finalizeExitedSessions` caps its eager condensing at `sweepCondenseBudget = time.Second` (session_finalize.go:31, applied at :54). The reason is stated in its own doc comment (:15-31): "the callers here are interactive commands — including `entire status --json`, which the MCP entire_status tool calls, where nothing prints until the sweep returns."

A post-upgrade backlog therefore drains at roughly one second of condensing per fifteen minutes.

The remaining sessions are not lost — they are marked ENDED (cheap, always happens) and PostCommit retries them — but that is the pre-existing behaviour, so for the ACTIVE-zombie half of the feature the new detached process buys latency isolation and very little throughput.

  --file cmd/entire/cli/session_sweep.go --line 232 \
  -m 'The throttle failure mode is "spawn every time", which is the thing the throttle exists to prevent.

```go
if commonDir, cerr := session.GetGitCommonDir(ctx); cerr == nil &&
    sweepRecentlySpawned(commonDir, time.Now()) {
    return
}
sweepSpawn(root)
```

A `GetGitCommonDir` error short-circuits the `&&`, so the throttle is skipped entirely and the spawn goes ahead — one detached child per session start, unbounded. The doc comment at :186-193 says the guard exists so "a burst of hooks (or an agent that restarts sessions rapidly) would [not] fork one child per hook", and the `recentlySpawnedMarker` comment inherited from the trail refresh says failures "fall through to spawning — never worse than before this guard existed". That is true for the trail refresh, where the marker was added to an already-shipped spawn; here the guard is the only thing bounding fork count for a brand-new spawn site, so falling open is a stronger concession than the borrowed comment implies.

`GetGitCommonDir` failing is also correlated with the sweep being useless (no resolvable repo), so failing closed loses nothing.

Fix: `commonDir, cerr := ...; if cerr != nil { return }` before the throttle check, or handle the error explicitly so the fall-open is a decision rather than a `&&` side effect.

Secondary, same line: the O(N) work at :223-228 (`ListSessionStates` over the shared dir, plus an `OwnerExited` proc probe per ACTIVE session) runs *before* the throttle check on every session start. Reordering is not free — `recentlySpawnedMarker` records on a miss (trail_context_cache.go:463), so checking it first would burn the window on a no-op check — but given the open hook-latency floor in this repo, the ordering deserves a comment saying it is deliberate and what a read-only variant would need.' 2>&1 | tail -5

content.text:
Posted. All anchors show `freshness: current` — I checked out each branch before posting so the file/line locations resolve against the branch tip rather than my review branch.

**Trail 1061** (#2013) — 5 findings + 1 comment thread:
- `manual_commit_hooks.go:1435` — **medium** — guest path resets the checkpoint window (`StepCount = 0`) but keeps the shadow branch and `BaseCommit`, so the same tip stays re-condensable and the session stops pinning its own branch
- `manual_commit_hooks.go:1428` — low — variadic `opts` defaults `isHome` to false, i.e. guest is the fail-open direction
- `session_identity.go:122` — low — raw `==` on worktree paths where the same package uses `filepath.Clean`
- `session_identity.go:42` — low — ambiguity hint fires once per replayed commit during a rebase
- `session_identity_test.go:348` — low — no pin on the guest branch of `condenseAndUpdateState` or the carry-forward gate
- Comment: the guest gate is path-based (so it also changes the pre-existing fallback path), and the 15-min liveness window converts a deliberate refusal into a guess — both belong in the description

**Trail 1073** (#2029) — 4 findings + 1 comment thread:
- `session_sweep.go:36` — **high** — `Phase.IsActive()` is `PhaseActive` only, so IDLE dead-owner sessions never nominate a sweep, even though `finalizeExitedSessions` inside the sweep does fix them; the new doc paragraph's justification ("matching doctor's boundary") is wrong since doctor calls the same function
- `session_sweep.go:97` — medium — detached sweep inherits `sweepCondenseBudget = 1s`, whose stated rationale is an interactive caller; with the 15-min throttle a backlog drains at ~1s per 15 min
- `session_sweep.go:232` — low — `GetGitCommonDir` error short-circuits the `&&` and skips the throttle entirely; plus a note on the O(N) work running before the throttle check
- `session_sweep_test.go:132` — low — the IDLE case has no `Owner`, so it passes on an empty fixture rather than on phase exclusion
- Comment: the two branches merge cleanly except one docs hunk, and `Owner` now carries three behaviours on an unmeasured resolve rate

@@ -751,7 +751,7 @@ The manual-commit strategy (`manual_commit*.go`) does not modify the active bran
 - **Location-independent transcript resolution** - transcript paths are always computed dynamically from the current repo location (via `agent.GetSessionDir` + `agent.ResolveSessionFile`), never stored in checkpoint metadata. This ensures restore/rewind works after repo relocation or across machines.
 - **Token usage scoping** - `SessionState.TokenUsage` is the session-wide total used by `entire status`; `SessionState.CheckpointTokenUsage` is the pending checkpoint delta since the last condensation. Checkpoint metadata must stay scoped to `CheckpointTranscriptStart` or the pending checkpoint delta. Cursor tokens come only from stop-hook payloads, while Copilot CLI can also backfill full-session totals from `session.shutdown`. Condensation's transcript recompute runs with `subagentsDir=""` and so drops `SubagentTokens`; `withSubagentTokensFrom` refills it from the already-rescoped `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`, and the store sums it across a checkpoint's sessions via `types.AddTokenUsage` (the single token-summing primitive — do not hand-roll another; a field-by-field copy is how the nested total came to be dropped in the first place).
 - Tracks session state in `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees)
-- **Commit-to-session linking is identity-first** (`strategy/session_identity.go`): identity comes from `SessionState.Owner`, the `proclive.Identity` that `captureSessionOwner` already records on every turn start (first non-transient ancestor — proclive skips shells, `entire` itself, and the Go toolchain, so a human commit typed in the same terminal never matches). Commit hooks snapshot their own ancestry once (`proclive.CurrentAncestry`) and match every candidate against it in memory (`Ancestry.Depth`) — one hostname/boot-id/proc walk per commit, not one per session state — linking the commit to the session whose agent process is an ancestor — in any worktree (nearest ancestor wins, so a nested agent beats the outer agent that spawned it, and only a tie at equal depth falls to the latest interaction; host/boot/start-time guards defeat PID reuse and cross-machine matches; Windows cannot introspect and falls back to worktree matching). The identity match is UNIONED with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement: a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree. A commit identity-matched outside the session's home worktree is guest-linked — condensed and linked, but worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`, shadow-branch realignment) is never mutated from a foreign worktree (`isSessionHomeWorktree`). Worktree matching is always computed (it is the sole mechanism for commits with no agent ancestry): imported sessions never link, and multi-worktree ambiguity is filtered to recently-interacting sessions (15 min) before declining — the stderr hint naming `entire session adopt` fires only from the commit-linking path, and only when identity matching could not rescue the commit either. Under `go test`, `session.NewStateStore` and `NewStateStoreForWorktree` refuse to open outside the temp root so non-isolated tests fail loudly instead of leaking fixture sessions into a real repo.
+- **Commit-to-session linking is identity-first** (`strategy/session_identity.go`): identity comes from `SessionState.Owner`, the `proclive.Identity` that `captureSessionOwner` already records on every turn start (first non-transient ancestor — proclive skips shells, `entire` itself, and the Go toolchain, so a human commit typed in the same terminal never matches). Commit hooks snapshot their own ancestry once (`proclive.CurrentAncestry`) and match every candidate against it in memory (`Ancestry.Depth`) — one hostname/boot-id/proc walk per commit, not one per session state — linking the commit to the session whose agent process is an ancestor — in any worktree (nearest ancestor wins, so a nested agent beats the outer agent that spawned it, and only a tie at equal depth falls to the latest interaction; host/boot/start-time guards defeat PID reuse and cross-machine matches; Windows cannot introspect and falls back to worktree matching). The identity match is UNIONED with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement: a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree. Any session matched outside its home worktree is guest-linked — whether identity-matched or selected by the pre-existing single-worktree fallback — and is condensed and linked without mutating worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`, shadow-branch realignment) from the foreign worktree (`isSessionHomeWorktree`). Worktree matching is always computed (it is the sole mechanism for commits with no agent ancestry): imported sessions never link, and multi-worktree ambiguity is filtered to recently-interacting sessions (15 min) before declining. This deliberately turns some former ambiguity declines into a best-candidate link; `recentSessionWindow` is a correctness tradeoff because a session in a long-running build or tool call can age out and leave the other recent worktree to win. The stderr hint naming `entire session adopt` fires only from the commit-linking path, and only when identity matching could not rescue the commit either. Under `go test`, `session.NewStateStore` and `NewStateStoreForWorktree` refuse to open outside the temp root so non-isolated tests fail loudly instead of leaking fixture sessions into a real repo.
 - **Reclaiming sessions whose agent vanished** - not every agent fires a session-end hook, and any agent can be killed before its hook runs, so a session can be left un-finalized forever. `SessionState.Owner` — the same fingerprint commit linking matches above — is captured at every turn start by `captureSessionOwner`, and `State.OwnerExited()` reports it gone via `proclive.Check`. `finalizeExitedSessions` sweeps those inside `entire status` (text and `--json`) and `entire doctor`, ending them exactly as a clean stop would. **`OwnerExited` deliberately covers IDLE as well as ACTIVE** — an agent that finishes its last turn and then quits leaves IDLE, so gating on ACTIVE alone missed the common case; only already-finalized sessions are excluded, per the shared `State.IsEnded()` predicate. Liveness is Unknown on Windows and for cross-host state, where behaviour degrades to the `StuckActiveThreshold` timeout. Because the sweep runs inside interactive commands, its eager condensing is capped by `sweepCondenseBudget` across the whole sweep: every candidate is always marked ENDED (a single atomic rename — that is what un-sticks it from `entire status`), while condensing runs only while the budget lasts, so a multi-day backlog drains over successive invocations instead of stalling one. Skipping a condense is the existing fail-open path — PostCommit retries, and `doctor` reports the session as "ended with uncondensed checkpoint data".
 - **Session-end hooks that run under a host deadline** - an agent whose session-end hook fires inside its own shutdown may be killed part-way through. Such agents declare `agent.SessionEndBudgeter` (Codex: 3s cap, process tree killed on expiry). The budget bounds **only** the eager condense in `endSessionNow`, so the cheap step that un-sticks the session is never the one given up on; it is set below the host cap with enough headroom for the shell wrapper and binary load, which happen before Entire's own clock starts. Unbounded is not the same as guaranteed, though: mark-ended runs under `MutateSessionState`, whose flock acquire blocks, so a concurrent condense holding the lock can push it past the cap and get the tree killed — the exited-owner sweep above is the backstop. content.text:
Re-reviewed both at their new tips. All nine findings are genuinely fixed — I verified each by reading the diff and running the tests, plus a mutation probe on the one that mattered most.

## 1061 (#2013) — tip `9fc73e026`

| Finding | Fix | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| StepCount pin | `pendingStepCount` restored after `resetCheckpointWindow` | Reverted the two lines → `TestPostCommit_GuestCondensationPreservesHomeShadowState` fails on the StepCount assertion, and the log confirms the guest condense ran. Non-vacuous. |
| Variadic `opts` | now positional `opts condenseOpts` | builds, single call site each |
| Raw `==` on paths | `filepath.Clean` both sides + `TestIsSessionHomeWorktree_CleansPaths` | pass |
| Rebase hint spam | `&& !isGitSequenceOperation(ctx)` + a `.git/rebase-merge` fixture test | pass |
| Test coverage gap | `TestPostCommit_GuestCondensationPreservesHomeShadowState` — end-to-end, asserts the shadow ref is byte-identical | pass |
| Both scope notes | landed in CLAUDE.md, the arch doc, **and** the `recentSessionWindow` constant comment | — |

**One correction to my own review.** I claimed the guest path re-condenses the same shadow content. That was wrong. `cpkg.WriteOptions` carries `FilesTouched` (names), the transcript, prompts and tasks — not the shadow tree's blobs — so a guest condense genuinely does not consume the home worktree's shadow content. Peyton's comment ("the checkpoint window was consumed, but the home worktree's shadow content was not") is accurate, and preserving the pin was the right fix rather than deleting the branch.

**One new, low observation.** `ef2deecf6` inverted `isSessionHomeWorktree` so an unknown path is now "not home". Right default for mutation safety, but a session with an empty `WorktreePath` that identity matching finds is now permanently a guest — `BaseCommit` frozen, shadow branch never released, `FilesTouched` never cleared, so it re-condenses on every commit — and it happens silently. `findSessionByCommitAncestry` is the only route in (the worktree fallback already does `if state.WorktreePath == "" { continue }`), so skipping empty-`WorktreePath` states there too would close it. Reachability is genuinely low — every current writer sets the field, so this is legacy state files only.

## 1073 (#2029) — tip `f4881a3c3`

| Finding | Fix | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| IDLE scoping | `if !st.IsEnded() { return st.OwnerExited() }` — exactly the shape `finalizeExitedSessions` uses | test fixture now carries `deadOwner` and asserts `want: true`; the false "matching doctor's boundary" doc line is gone |
| Condense budget | `finalizeExitedSessions(ctx, states, condenseDeadline)`; sweep passes `time.Time{}`, status/doctor pass `interactiveSweepCondenseBudget`. `endSessionNow` already treats zero as unbounded (`!condenseDeadline.IsZero()`), and the scanner-failure path still forces `time.Now()` to skip | tests pass |
| Throttle fail-open | resolves the common dir first and returns on error; added a `sweepGitCommonDir` seam and a test asserting zero spawns; my secondary point about the discovery/throttle ordering is now an explicit comment naming the read-only-marker prerequisite | pass |

They also went past the findings: imported sessions are now excluded from `finalizeExitedSessions` itself (`isExitedSessionFinalizationCandidate`), and `f4881a3c3` aligned the predicate with `IsCondensableEndedSession` on `(StepCount <= 0 && !HasTaskContent())`.

**Two new, low observations:**

1. `session_sweep.go:46` — after `if !st.IsEnded() { … }` three lines above, `st.Phase != session.PhaseEnded` can only be true for the half-ended shape (`EndedAt` set, `Phase` still IDLE) that `IsEnded`'s own doc exists to normalize — "a state file can carry one without the other (a legacy record, or a partial write)". Such a state is dropped here, skipped by `finalizeExitedSessions` (because `OwnerExited` returns false once `IsEnded`), and falls into `classifySession`'s `default: return nil`. So it's invisible to both sweep halves *and* doctor, and only the 7-day purge reaches it — which deletes rather than condenses. The function now contradicts itself on exactly the case it just started getting right.

2. `proclive.Check` re-reads `os.Hostname()` and `bootID()` per identity, with no memoization — on Linux that's a `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` read plus a `/proc/<pid>/stat` read every call. Widening the candidate set from ACTIVE to all non-ended is correct, but it also widened this: in my clone that's **33** `Check` calls per session start, up from 3. Sub-millisecond each, so not a blocker — but it's now on the hook path, it scales with the state-file count (which grows to the 7-day threshold), and `proclive` already has the right pattern in `CurrentAncestry` (resolve host/boot once, match in memory). A `Prober`/`CheckAll` would mirror it.

## Status

Both merge cleanly except the same one docs hunk in `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` (both still insert at the same anchor). All CI green on both; the only failing check is `Entire Gates`, and its detail is `Approvals: failed — No reviewers have approved this trail` — Checks and Findings both pass.

Want me to post the three new observations as findings, or leave them here?

content.text:
Yes, I think it's the right call — with two qualifications.

**Why merging now is right.** None of the three remaining findings is a regression against main. Two are only reachable through legacy state files (an empty `WorktreePath`, or an `EndedAt`-without-`PhaseEnded` partial write) that no current writer can produce, and the third is pure perf. Both PRs are well-tested — I mutation-probed the guest-condensation test and it genuinely fails when the fix is reverted, which is more than most tests in this area can claim. Holding two reviewed, green PRs on legacy-only edge cases would be the wrong trade.

**Qualification 1: don't merge them back-to-back.** Land 1061, give it a few days of dogfooding, then 1073. Not ritual caution — 1061 changes commit→session attribution for *every* commit in *every* repo, and the failure mode is a wrong or dangling checkpoint trailer, which is precisely the bug class this repo has been chasing. If something's off you want one suspect, not two. You also get the conflict resolution for free: 1073 has to take a main merge and resolve that docs hunk anyway once 1061 lands.

**Qualification 2: trim the follow-up to two fixes, not three.** The two one-liners are worth doing (`isSessionHomeWorktree` skipping empty-`WorktreePath` states at the identity matcher, and `isSweepableZombie:46` not silently dropping the half-ended shape). The `proclive.Check` memoization I'd leave as a comment on the code, not a change — it's a few hundred microseconds against an open ~3-second p50 hook-latency floor. Fixing it now is optimising the wrong end.

**The thing actually worth doing instead** is the `Owner` resolve-rate question from my 1073 comment, which nobody has answered. Both features are load-bearing on a field that's nil on Windows and nil whenever hook ancestry resolves to only transient processes — and if it resolves poorly on some agent, that agent silently gets none of this. I have one data point from measuring my own clone while reviewing: **33 of 34 non-ended sessions carry an `Owner`**. Encouraging, but that's one machine with a Claude Code-heavy mix. A short script across a few teammates' state dirs, bucketed by `agent_type`, would tell you whether these two PRs are load-bearing or decorative for Cursor, Codex, Copilot CLI and Droid. That's more valuable than any of the three findings.

Want me to go ahead on that basis — approve and merge 1061 now, queue 1073 for later in the week?

content.text:
Two things to correct before the plan — and your reasoning about approval is exactly right, for a reason worth naming.

**The trail numbers are swapped.** It's the other way round:

- **1073 / #2029 (zombie sweep) is MERGED** — by you at 11:11:33Z, merge commit `875a2b6ae`, branch auto-deleted.
- **1061 / #2013 (identity linking) is still OPEN**, `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, branch `feat/session-identity-linking` at `9fc73e026`.

So the one needing the conflict resolution is the identity-linking PR, and it now conflicts with main *because* the sweep landed first. I re-tested: one conflicted file, `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md`, nothing else.

**And you're right that you can't do both.** The `main` ruleset has `require_last_push_approval: true` — whoever makes the most recent push cannot be the approving reviewer. Plus `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: true`, so approving first and then pushing wouldn't work either. It's structural, not a workaround problem.

Also worth knowing from that same ruleset: the required checks are only `test`, `lint`, and `check-licenses / license-check`. **`Entire Gates` is not a required check** — its failure was never what was blocking the merge. The approval rule was.

So the split has to be: someone else pushes, you approve.

options.description: I merge main into the branch, resolve the hunk, and push under your git identity. Then you need a third teammate to approve the result, since require_last_push_approval will exclude you.

options.label: Admin bypass
options.description: You have admin, so the ruleset can be bypassed: I resolve and push, then merge without an approving review. Fastest, but it skips the approval rule rather than satisfying it, on a PR that changes commit attribution in every repo.

<<<<<<< HEAD
#### Commit-to-session linking

The commit hooks (prepare-commit-msg / post-commit) resolve which sessions a
commit belongs to via `findSessionsForCommitLinking`
(`strategy/session_identity.go`): the **worktree-matched set** (every session
with pending content in the commit's worktree — concurrent sessions interleave
by design) **plus the identity-matched session** when the committing process's
ancestry names one that path matching missed.

**Identity matching**: reuses the owner fingerprint liveness already
records — `SessionState.Owner`, a `proclive.Identity` captured on every turn
start by `captureSessionOwner` (the first non-transient ancestor of the hook:
agents run hooks as children, possibly via `sh -c`, and proclive skips
shells, the `entire` binary itself, and the Go toolchain). At commit time the
hook snapshots its ancestry once (`proclive.CurrentAncestry`) and asks
`Ancestry.Depth(owner)` per candidate: was this commit's process spawned,
however indirectly, by that session's agent? Snapshotting once matters — the
shared store holds one state file per session, so a per-candidate walk would
repeat the hostname, boot-id, and proc reads dozens of times per commit.
Host, boot, and start-time guards mean a recycled PID or an identity recorded
on another machine can never match. The nearest ancestor wins, so a nested
agent is attributed over the outer agent that spawned it; only sessions
matching at the same depth (one agent process hosting several sessions) fall
back to the most recently interacting one. On platforms proclive cannot introspect (Windows),
identity matching reports nothing and linking falls back to worktree
matching. This makes an agent-made commit link to
its own session **in any worktree**, with no bookkeeping to drift. Any session
matched outside its home worktree is **guest-linked**, whether it came from
identity matching or the pre-existing single-worktree fallback below: it
condenses and links, but never mutates worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`,
shadow-branch realignment) — those follow only the session's own worktree HEAD.

**Worktree matching** (always computed; the sole mechanism for commits with
no recorded agent in their ancestry — human commits, detached runners): exact
`WorktreePath` match first, then sessions from a sibling worktree of the same
repo, provided they resolve to a single worktree. Imported sessions (`Kind=imported`) never link —
they are historical records. When candidates span several worktrees, sessions
that interacted within the last 15 minutes are preferred; if a single live
worktree remains it links, otherwise the hook declines with a stderr hint
naming `entire session adopt` (two genuinely live sessions in different
worktrees are never guessed between). This liveness filter intentionally turns
some cases the old code declined outright into a best-candidate link. The
15-minute `recentSessionWindow` is therefore a correctness tradeoff: a session
in a long-running build or tool call can age out, allowing the remaining recent
worktree to win.

Under `go test`, the session state store refuses to open outside the temp
root (both `session.NewStateStore` and `NewStateStoreForWorktree`), so a test
missing repo isolation fails loudly instead of leaking fixture sessions into
a real repo's `.git/entire-sessions` — leaked fixtures once hijacked commit
linking and produced a dangling `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.
=======
**Background zombie sweep.** The session-start hook checks the shared
session-state directory for zombies — non-ended sessions whose owning agent
process has exited (including the common IDLE case), and ENDED sessions that
still hold uncondensed checkpoint data more than 24h after ending (younger ones
are left alone so PostCommit carry-forward keeps its chance). When any exist,

#### Commit-to-session linking

The commit hooks (prepare-commit-msg / post-commit) resolve which sessions a
commit belongs to via `findSessionsForCommitLinking`

with pending content in the commit's worktree — concurrent sessions interleave
by design) **plus the identity-matched session** when the committing process's
ancestry names one that path matching missed.

**Identity matching**: reuses the owner fingerprint liveness already
records — `SessionState.Owner`, a `proclive.Identity` captured on every turn
start by `captureSessionOwner` (the first non-transient ancestor of the hook:
agents run hooks as children, possibly via `sh -c`, and proclive skips
shells, the `entire` binary itself, and the Go toolchain). At commit time the
hook snapshots its ancestry once (`proclive.CurrentAncestry`) and asks
`Ancestry.Depth(owner)` per candidate: was this commit's process spawned,
however indirectly, by that session's agent? Snapshotting once matters — the
shared store holds one state file per session, so a per-candidate walk would
repeat the hostname, boot-id, and proc reads dozens of times per commit.
Host, boot, and start-time guards mean a recycled PID or an identity recorded
on another machine can never match. The nearest ancestor wins, so a nested
agent is attributed over the outer agent that spawned it; only sessions
matching at the same depth (one agent process hosting several sessions) fall
back to the most recently interacting one. On platforms proclive cannot introspect (Windows),
identity matching reports nothing and linking falls back to worktree
matching. This makes an agent-made commit link to
its own session **in any worktree**, with no bookkeeping to drift. Any session
matched outside its home worktree is **guest-linked**, whether it came from
identity matching or the pre-existing single-worktree fallback below: it
condenses and links, but never mutates worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`,
shadow-branch realignment) — those follow only the session's own worktree HEAD.

**Worktree matching** (always computed; the sole mechanism for commits with
no recorded agent in their ancestry — human commits, detached runners): exact
`WorktreePath` match first, then sessions from a sibling worktree of the same
repo, provided they resolve to a single worktree. Imported sessions (`Kind=imported`) never link —
they are historical records. When candidates span several worktrees, sessions
that interacted within the last 15 minutes are preferred; if a single live
worktree remains it links, otherwise the hook declines with a stderr hint
